module.title: HTML basics
module.description: Tags, structure and your very first web page.

ex0.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Hello, we are your new clients. We would like to have a nice website for our future shop. The name of our shop is “Lost and Found”.
dialogue1: It would be so nice to have a really big heading with the name on it!
dialogue2: We need a description too. How about, right under the title, a paragraph? What should it say?
dialogue3: “Welcome to Lost and Found, where you can find what you've lost and lose what you've found!”
hint0: Do you need help? I'm here for you! For this first exercise, why not just try using tags and see what they do?
hint1: If you struggle, don't hesitate to also reach out to your neighbors!
ex0.check2: The paragraph is still there and says “Welcome to Lost and Found, where you can find what you've lost and lose what you've found!”
ex0.check3: The title comes before the paragraph
ex0.lesson:
<html>, <head>, <body>, <p> and <h1> are called tags. Most tags go in pairs: the opening one (<html>) and the closing one (</html>).

There are 3 fundamental tags:

  • <html> wraps the whole page and announces that the rest is HTML.
  • <head> contains metadata: information for the browser, not visible on the page.
  • <body> contains everything visible on the page.

For now we focus on the body and leave the head empty.

ex1.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: That's a good start. Now the customers should be able to see what kind of products we actually sell, right?
dialogue1: Our site should have different sections, one for the items we sell, another one for ordering...
dialogue2: Let's start slowly with only one
dialogue3: We need a section and inside, there should be another heading. The heading should be smaller than the title but bigger than the paragraph
dialogue4: The heading should say “Our items”. Then we will be able to list what we sell!
hint0: A section is defined with the tag <div>!
hint1: Headings go from h1 to h6. h1 defines the most important, h6 defines the least important
ex1.check0: There is a heading inside a section
ex1.check2: The new section is after the title and the paragraph

ex2.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Amazing! Time to add the other sections!
dialogue1: Just like the “Our items” section, we want one that says “FAQ”. In case our customers have questions!
dialogue2: Right after, it should be the “Order” section. After all, it's pointless if our customers can't even order anything...
dialogue3: The sections should follow each other in the right order, be careful!
hint0: You just need to do what you've already done
ex2.check0: There are three sections with the right heading inside
ex2.check3: The sections are in the right order

ex3.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Now it's time to actually make a list of what we are selling. Why don't you do that for us?
dialogue1: You should start with another section that you will put inside the “Our items” section. This new section should have a heading and a paragraph.
dialogue2: Hey, it would be better if the new heading is smaller than the previous one!
dialogue3: Now the heading should be the item sold. For example it could say “Toothpaste”
dialogue4: The paragraph should contain the description of the item. You could write “Some ancient toothpaste with a weird scent. Its yellow color might not be the original one. Who knows how long it has been here?”
dialogue5: It's time to get creative! Just imagine items and their description and have fun with them! We sell whatever you could imagine! Try to have at least two items. Feel free to add more though!
hint0: Try to use the heading <h3> this time!
ex3.check0: There are at least two sections composed of a heading and a paragraph
ex3.check1: The sections are inside the “Our items” section and under the heading
ex3.check2: The new headings are not empty and have another text than the default one
ex3.check3: The new paragraphs are not empty and have another text than the default one

ex4.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: You know what? I think it's missing something... But I can't think of anything
dialogue1: I know! There should be at least one image! It would be better if our customers could have a visual on the product they want to buy
dialogue2: That's an excellent idea. We should put it between the title of the item and its description
dialogue3: There are some images ready to be used in the images tab, on the left panel, but feel free to import yours
hint0: Change the src inside the image tag to choose another image
ex4.check1: The image is placed between the <h3> heading and the paragraph tag

ex5.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Oh no! We've got an emergency! Someone asked for my profile card but it's not done yet!
dialogue1: I fail to see how it is an emergency?
dialogue2: We could lose a potential customer! I need my card done. It's way too ugly
dialogue3: Your card is not done yet because it's empty!
dialogue4: Time to do some css! Please center the heading and all paragraphs
hint0: If HTML is the structure of the page, CSS is the style!
hint1: Select the tag you want to stylize then add properties
ex5.lesson: HTML structures the page, while CSS takes care of the style. You link a CSS file to a HTML file with the tag <link>, that should be put inside the <head>.

ex6.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Hum, I wanted to add an image... but I might have made a mistake
dialogue1: Why is your image so big?! We need to resize it!
dialogue2: It should be smaller so it fits in your card... How about making it 100px x 100px?
dialogue3: It should also be centered, like the heading and the paragraphs
dialogue4: It would be really nice if there was a way to make it round too...
hint0: When it comes to CSS, sometimes searching the internet is the best way... after asking your neighbors!
ex6.check1: The image is 100px wide and 100px high

ex7.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Gabbro, your card is starting to look like an actual card. I think your job should be written in bold though. And in blue. And bigger too but not too big
dialogue1: I think my image should have a colored border
dialogue3: The description would look great if it stayed the same but in italic
hint0: You have learned that you can select an element by their tag, but you can do the same with classes!
ex7.check1: The first paragraph is in blue, bold and has a size between 20px and 25px
ex7.check2: The second paragraph is simply in italic

ex8.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: To finish this card so we can go back to our website, we should actually make it look like a card, right?
dialogue1: It's time to put everything inside a rectangle. Let's add borders to the div
dialogue2: A background color would be nice
dialogue3: Of course the elements inside the div should be centered inside the div
dialogue4: They should not be too close to the borders though. Let's add some space between the elements inside the div and the borders of the div
dialogue5: The div itself should be centered
hint0: Margin is the space between the element and everything around it, padding is the space between the element and everything inside the element
ex8.check0: Add a background color to the section
ex8.check1: Add a border to the div
ex8.check2: Add a space between the borders of the div and the elements inside the div
ex8.check4: The elements inside the div are centered

ex9.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Thank you for the help with my card! I was able to give it to a potential customer
dialogue1: You know, now that we had to make your card look better, I'm starting to think it would be nice to add more style to our website too...
dialogue2: First, it's necessary to connect the html file with the css file. Add <link rel='stylesheet' href='style.css'> inside the head tag. To edit the head tag, use the code mode instead of the blocks one
dialogue3: How about centering the main heading and the first paragraph, the one that describes our shop?
dialogue4: I think we should have a background color too. Or an image?
hint0: Your head should look like this: <head><link rel='stylesheet' href='style.css'></head> now
hint1: To add a background color, you should put the background-color property on the highest tag...
ex9.check0: Link your css file with your html file
ex9.check3: Add a background color or image

ex10.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: Mmmh... I think it would be better if the title had another color. How about putting both the title and the description of our shop inside a section and change the section background color?
dialogue1: Oh and the borders of the new section should be rounded. And how about having the description in italic instead of normal style?
dialogue2: Aren't you asking for a lot at once?
dialogue3: I wasn't done yet... I think it would be even better if there were space between the text and the borders
dialogue4: And the heading and paragraph should have their own text color! White? Something that would look great with the new section background color!
hint0: Feel free to add the class attribute!
hint1: Class is added to a tag like this <div class='[name of class]'>
ex10.check0: The main heading and the shop description are inside a section
ex10.check1: The background color of the title section is different from the rest of the page
ex10.check2: The text color of the title and the description is different from the rest of the page
ex10.check5: There is space between the text and the borders of the section
ex10.check6: The heading and the description are centered inside the section

ex11.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: The title looks nice now. Time to take care of the items section!
dialogue1: Each item section should have the same background color or image. And it should be different from the general background, of course
dialogue2: And they must have visible borders too, of a different color than both the general background and the section background
dialogue3: The image, if there is one, should of course be resized to fit inside the section if it's too big
dialogue4: And the description of the items should be in italic!
dialogue5: I feel like your requests keep getting worse... So I added an example of what an item section could look like
hint0: Don't forget to ask your neighbors if you feel stuck!
ex11.check0: Every item subsection inside the “Our items” section has visible borders
ex11.check1: They all have the same background color, different from the rest of the page background and different from the title section background
ex11.check2: The item description is in italic
ex11.check3: Images fit inside their item section
ex11.check4: There is space between the item sections and also between their borders and their content

ex12.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: It's not perfect but it gets better at least
dialogue1: We can move on to the next section, the FAQ. Ideally it would be multiple questions and you could click on each to show or hide the answer. I wonder if it's possible...
dialogue2: The questions should be in bold and there should be a background color too... oh and the answer should be a paragraph!
dialogue3: I've once more added an example...
dialogue4: It would be so great if the pointer of the mouse changed when hovering over a question, to show it's clickable...
hint0: Perhaps you should consider the tags <details> and <summary>
ex12.check0: There is at least one question and answer
ex12.check1: The questions have a background color

ex13.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue0: It's time to take care of the last section, the order one!
dialogue1: We need multiple fields: two text fields, a date field and a check box
dialogue2: The text fields should ask for the customer name and email. The date field is for the delivery date and the check box for them to agree to our conditions
dialogue3: There should also be a button to confirm...
hint0: Use the <form> tag for this exercise!
hint1: For fields, perhaps the <input> tag, paired with the <label> tag, could be interesting...
ex13.check0: There is a text field for the name
ex13.check1: There is a text field for the email
ex13.check2: There is a date field for the delivery date

ex14.title: Hello and welcome
dialogue2: Why don't you do whatever you want now? Have fun! You can add a menu, more items, whatever you want!
